metadata.title: Install Tovli Skills in Codex and Claude

overview.objective: Users can install any of the four published Tovli skills in Codex or Claude through a native plugin marketplace or by asking the agent to install from the GitHub repository.
overview.user_need: People should be able to browse an installable plugin or paste the repository link into their coding agent and get working skills in the intended scope.
overview.today: The installer source is public at tag v0.1.0 (d3bf3d7). GitHub hosts the three separate marketplace branches. Both CLI marketplace routes and the standalone installer passed fresh installs from GitHub.
overview.plain_language_solution: Distribute four skills through three named marketplaces and a small installer either agent can run from a checkout. Both routes use the same skill sources and launch on Codex CLI and Claude Code. List desktop routes after verification.
overview.why_now: Installation currently depends on users finding the correct destination and copying complete skill folders themselves.

plan_now.current_agreed_plan: The three marketplaces and checkout installer are live on GitHub. Codex CLI 0.171.0 and Claude Code 2.1.322 installed all three public packages and reported the expected four skills. The installer installed all four from a fresh v0.1.0 checkout for both clients. The authenticated chat-driven prompt and desktop install routes remain unverified.

visual_examples.title: What a user could paste into either agent
visual_examples.description: Install Tovli Skills from https://github.com/Tovli/Tovli-skills for this project. Use the repo installer and tell me how to invoke the skills. To install one skill, name it in the request. If scope is omitted, the agent asks the user to choose project or user scope.

visual_examples.title: Three independently addable marketplaces
visual_examples.description: tovli-planning contains tovli-plan and tovli-agentic-planner. tovli-explainer contains tovli-explain. tovli-writer contains tovli-post-writer. Each catalog is generated as a self-contained local package and uses an independent marketplace/<name> Git branch.

user_journey.action: Choose marketplace installation or ask the agent to install from the repo link.
user_journey.response: Users add one of the three named marketplaces. The repo README points an agent to the cross-platform installer and the public skill names.
user_journey.outcome: Users can select a named marketplace or start the installer from the source repo.

user_journey.action: Select the plugin or named skills and use the intended installation scope.
user_journey.response: Marketplace installs use native client controls. For a repo-link install, the agent asks for scope if omitted, then runs the installer from a checkout with the chosen client, skills and scope.
user_journey.outcome: The expected skills and their supporting files are installed at the requested scope.

user_journey.action: Open a fresh session in the target project and invoke a skill.
user_journey.response: The client discovers the skill. The installer reports installed names, source revision, scope and invocation. The native route identifies its marketplace and package.
user_journey.outcome: The user can verify that the chosen skill is ready to use.

edge_cases.scenario: A user asks for tovli-explain and the source folder has a different name.
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Resolve git-branch-change-explainer to the public name tovli-explain and install it under the public name with its supporting files.

edge_cases.scenario: A standalone copy or a plugin containing the same skill already exists.
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Report the matching installation and scope. An identical rerun reports success. For divergent standalone files, preserve them and report the conflict with an explicit update or replacement path.

edge_cases.scenario: An agent can read GitHub but lacks local writes or shell access.
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Report the blocked action and provide the verified native command or client control for the user's environment.

edge_cases.scenario: The user omits scope in a repo-link install request.
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Ask whether to install for the project or the user. Wait for the answer before writing to a destination. A direct noninteractive installer run with missing scope reports the options and exits before writes.

edge_cases.scenario: A skill's Python or project prerequisites are missing.
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Document installer prerequisites separately from the prerequisites for running each skill. Report missing installer prerequisites before copying any skill.

edge_cases.scenario: A user registers all three marketplaces in the same profile.
edge_cases.expected_behavior: All three coexist under their own names. Each package contains its assigned skills and supports independent update and removal.

success_measures.target: All three marketplaces install and coexist on Codex CLI and Claude Code. The standalone installer can install one selected skill or the collection on either client.
success_measures.measured_by: A test matrix records client version, OS, source revision, scope, expected skills, and actual result.

success_measures.target: Each baseline client can install one skill and all four from separate clean projects using the repo link. Omitted scope prompts for the user's choice before destination writes.
success_measures.measured_by: Observe the agent follow the guide, place complete directories in scope, and report how to invoke the skills.

success_measures.target: All four skills are discoverable. The planning and branch report skills render valid HTML from their installed copies on each baseline client and route.
success_measures.measured_by: Exercise both script-based skills in sample projects and check installed support-file integrity.

success_measures.target: Same-version reinstalls are repeatable, each marketplace updates independently, and unrelated local skills survive removal or conflict handling.
success_measures.measured_by: Verify lifecycle behavior at the documented scopes with clean and pre-populated fixtures.

assumptions.statement: The public release should distribute the four catalog entries from the top-level source directories.
assumptions.evidence: Release v0.1.0 packages the four canonical skill directories at d3bf3d7. The workspace-local planning copy and unpublished working-tree edits were excluded.

assumptions.statement: Windows and one POSIX environment provide a practical initial test matrix for the supported local clients.
assumptions.evidence: The distribution regression suite passed on Windows and Ubuntu WSL. The native CLI marketplace fixtures ran in isolated Ubuntu profiles.

assumptions.statement: Distinct Git refs in the same repo can host the three marketplace identities.
assumptions.evidence: Both CLI versions registered and installed all three branch-backed marketplaces from the public GitHub repository. Disposable profiles also verified refresh and independent removal.

questions.question: How should the marketplace group the four skills?
questions.today: The README lists four separate skills. Both clients' package models can carry multiple skills.
questions.why_it_matters: Plugin IDs, installation commands, and update granularity depend on the grouping.
questions.what_we_get: The selected groups let users install and update planning, explainer, and writer skills separately.
questions.if_we_skip_it: Plugin IDs and release packaging remain provisional.

options.description: Ship one tovli-skills plugin per client containing the four skills.
options.tradeoff: Marketplace users receive all four and update them together.

options.description: Publish four individually installable plugins in each marketplace.
options.tradeoff: Users can choose just one. Each plugin adds metadata, install checks, and update coverage.

options.description: Publish both the collection and individual marketplace plugins.
options.tradeoff: Users get both choices in the catalog. Overlapping installs need explicit naming and duplicate handling.

options.description: Publish tovli-planning with tovli-plan and tovli-agentic-planner; tovli-explainer with tovli-explain; and tovli-writer with tovli-post-writer.
options.tradeoff: Three groups allow separate selection and updates, with additional packaging and validation compared with one bundle.

questions.note: The answer named three marketplaces. The plan treats them as three separately addable catalog identities. One package per catalog is the proposed implementation.

questions.question: What should the agent use when given the repo link?
questions.today: Both clients load standalone skills from client-specific directories. GitHub CLI documents gh skill for both clients, while the installed gh 2.57.0 here lacks that command.
questions.why_it_matters: The choice determines which environments can install from a prompt and what installer code needs maintenance.
questions.what_we_get: The selected installer centralizes skill selection, scope handling, safe copying, and reporting.
questions.if_we_skip_it: The repo-link flow depends on the agent improvising file placement and conflict behavior.

options.description: Document a Git checkout and safe file copy as the baseline, with gh skill as an optional shortcut after discovery and path checks pass.
options.tradeoff: The guide owns scope, name mapping, and conflict behavior. No custom installer is required for the first release.

options.description: Ship a small cross-platform installer invoked from a checked-out repository.
options.tradeoff: The installer can centralize selection, upgrades, rollback, and reporting. It adds an executable and runtime to support.

options.description: Make gh skill the standalone installer and require a compatible GitHub CLI.
options.tradeoff: Uses upstream install and update commands. Users with older binaries need an upgrade, and repository discovery must be demonstrated.

questions.note: The installer is invoked from a checked-out repository.

questions.question: Which client surfaces should be part of first-release support?
questions.today: Codex CLI 0.171.0 and Claude Code 2.1.322 are available locally. Official docs describe separate desktop install surfaces and skill discovery differs across local and hosted environments.
questions.why_it_matters: Support claims depend on where both routes can be installed and exercised with the required runtime.
questions.what_we_get: The first release has a concrete test baseline. Desktop support can be documented per surface once tested.
questions.if_we_skip_it: The release could imply support for clients where local writes or repo marketplaces are unavailable.

options.description: Require both routes on Codex CLI and Claude Code. List desktop routes once each has been verified.
options.tradeoff: Keeps CLI coverage a firm launch gate. Desktop capabilities can ship as verified additions.

options.description: Require Codex CLI, Claude Code, Codex desktop, and Claude desktop at launch, with a documented path for every advertised route.
options.tradeoff: More users have a tested entry point. Desktop availability and runtime differences may change the release scope or timing.

defaults.question: What scope should the repo-link flow use when a user names no scope?

options.description: Use project scope when the current project is unambiguous and report the destination.
options.tradeoff: Confines the install to the project. Other projects need their own install.

options.description: Ask for scope any time it is omitted.
options.tradeoff: Avoids an implicit choice and adds a step to each unspecified request.

direct_decisions.statement: Plan for both an installable plugin route and an agent-driven installation from the repository link.
direct_decisions.rationale: Both entry points are part of the requested outcome.
Both client families were requested. D-003 records the approved first-release surfaces.

out_this_round.description: Vendor directory submissions and organization-managed deployment
out_this_round.reason: The launch can use self-hosted Git marketplaces. Vendor directory publication adds a separate review and delivery process.
out_this_round.revisit_when: Revisit if public directory discovery or managed deployment becomes a requirement.

out_this_round.description: Changes to the skills' core workflows
out_this_round.reason: Packaging and client-facing invocation docs are enough for the requested outcome unless smoke tests expose a portability issue.
out_this_round.revisit_when: Address a concrete runtime portability issue found by the release test matrix.

phases.title: Inventory skills and verify client contracts
phases.outcome: Record the four skill source mappings and verify a Git distribution layout for three marketplace identities.
phases.done_when: The inventory explains the tovli-explain folder mismatch and the workspace-local tovli-plan copy. In both CLI clients, a disposable fixture verifies registering, installing, refreshing and removing three distinct names in one profile. Test distinct refs in one repo first and record the working layout and CLI versions.

phases.title: Build the three native marketplaces
phases.outcome: Generate three independently addable catalogs and packages for both clients from the same skill sources.
phases.done_when: Each marketplace has its own name and resolvable Codex and Claude catalog. tovli-planning contains tovli-plan and tovli-agentic-planner, tovli-explainer contains tovli-explain, and tovli-writer contains tovli-post-writer. Manifest checks pass and rerunning the build reproduces the catalogs and exact package contents.

phases.title: Build the cross-platform repo installer
phases.outcome: Enable standalone skill installs from a checkout at a known Git revision.
phases.done_when: The installer accepts the target client, one or more named skills or the collection, and explicit project or user scope. The agent asks when scope is omitted. A noninteractive installer run with missing scope exits before writes. The installer copies complete skill folders, reports destination, revision and invocation, and handles retry, interruption and divergent files without leaving a partial skill.

phases.title: Publish installation instructions in the repo
phases.outcome: Make the README the entry point for humans and agents and provide a single INSTALL.md guide.
phases.done_when: The README links the three named marketplaces and shows verified commands for both CLI clients. It includes a paste-ready repo-link prompt and links INSTALL.md. The guide covers prerequisites, scope, skill selection, invocation, update and removal. Desktop instructions are included for verified routes.

phases.title: Test both install routes on clean clients
phases.outcome: Capture an installation and exercise record for the approved client matrix.
phases.done_when: All three marketplace identities can be added and installed together with exactly the expected skills. For both required CLIs, verify discovery, invocation using installed assets, retry, update and removal. Exercise one-skill and collection installs in both scopes and verify that omitted scope prompts before writes.

phases.title: Release and verify from GitHub
phases.outcome: Publish the three marketplaces and the installer from the Tovli Skills source repo and verify the public routes.
phases.done_when: The release check detects catalog and package drift. The public README identifies the three Git sources and matching installer revision. Fresh installs from the public distribution succeed on both CLI clients and the prior known-good release remains available.

how_we_test_it.environment: Windows Python 3.14 and Ubuntu WSL Python 3.12 for the distribution suite. Codex CLI 0.171.0 and Claude Code 2.1.322 ran native checks inside disposable Ubuntu profiles. Claude also passed strict local catalog and manifest checks on Windows.
scenarios: Verified Git marketplace add with Codex --ref and Claude #ref for all three marketplace/<name> branches in a disposable fixture.
Verified actual generated skill membership, native discovery, catalog refresh and independent removal. Ran both installed Python renderers without the source checkout in the working directory.

Verified standalone scopes for both clients in disposable Ubuntu profiles. The Windows suite covered project scope and a separate Windows smoke passed user scope with a temporary home path. The authenticated repo-link prompt remains part of public release verification.

Verified Windows and POSIX path handling, missing noninteractive scope, retry and local edit protection. Codex discovered standalone skills at both scopes. Claude validated both standalone skill directories offline.
Remove the temporary checkout. Initialize a plan and render a branch report from the installed scripts. Discover and invoke the two Markdown-only skills.
Retry the same release, exercise an interrupted copy and a divergent existing skill, switch revisions and uninstall while preserving unrelated files.

Fresh installs from the public GitHub sources passed on both CLIs. A fresh checkout at v0.1.0 installed all four skills for both clients. Authenticated chat-driven install behavior remains unverified.
acceptance_criteria: All three marketplaces and the standalone route pass on Codex CLI and Claude Code. Each advertised desktop route has its own evidence.
All four skill names resolve in a fresh session, and bundled scripts and their relative assets work from the installed location.
The documented install report identifies the client, destination or plugin ID, installed skills, source revision, and any user action still needed.

where_it_ships.target: The public Tovli/Tovli-skills repository, three separately registered Git-backed marketplaces, the cross-platform installer, README and INSTALL.md.
where_it_ships.release_order: Verify catalog hosting in a disposable fixture. Build the marketplaces and installer, document the verified commands, run clean-client checks, then publish and retest.
where_it_ships.release_trigger: All three marketplace installs and the installer pass on Codex CLI and Claude Code. List desktop routes that passed.
where_it_ships.rollout_strategy: One marketplace/<name> Git branch per catalog in the existing public repository. Both client catalogs and their plugin package share a release tree generated from a committed source snapshot. Registration of this layout was verified in disposable profiles. Publish the source commit or tag for standalone installs and verify the public branches.
where_it_ships.rollback: Retain the last working revision of each marketplace and the installer. Document restoring a single catalog or using an earlier standalone release while preserving unrelated installs and local edits.

how_it_is_built.approach: Use one mapping from canonical skill folders to public names and marketplaces. Generate a self-contained package for each marketplace with skills/<public-name> and client manifests. Each marketplace root carries a Codex catalog at .agents/plugins/marketplace.json and a Claude catalog at .claude-plugin/marketplace.json. The installer reads the same skill mapping and resolves the client and explicit scope before writing.
quality_gates: Validate both client schemas across all three marketplaces. Check exact skill membership and compare generated package files against the shared source mapping.
Keep skill assets usable through relative paths from the installed SKILL.md. Exclude workspace copies and transient outputs from the release.
Native catalogs install skill files without install hooks. Standalone installs preserve unrelated files and respect managed client policies and requested permissions.
Check scope handling so an omitted choice cannot trigger a destination write.
handoffs: Inventory provides the public names, source roots, prerequisites, and client command versions required by the package and standalone routes.
Packaging and standalone installers provide reproducible entry points to the README and client-matrix checks.
Release documentation records the scope, tested versions, commands, and recovery steps observed in the matrix.

technical_implications.today: The root README defers paths to the agent.
technical_implications.proposed_change: Use PROJECT/.agents/skills or ~/.agents/skills for Codex, and PROJECT/.claude/skills or ~/.claude/skills for Claude Code. Require an explicit scope choice and use the public skill name for the installed folder.

technical_implications.today: Some skill READMEs use Codex-specific invocation and display metadata.
technical_implications.proposed_change: Preserve Codex metadata where useful. Document explicit Codex skill selection and test Claude Code slash names for standalone and namespaced plugin installation.

technical_implications.today: The catalog lives in root directories and the repo carries an extra tovli-plan workspace copy.
technical_implications.proposed_change: Generate three marketplace roots with each client's catalog and the approved skill membership. Keep the workspace-local tovli-plan outside the public payload. Use the same public source folders for packaging and the installer.

risks.description: Marketplace hosting or permissions can differ between the disposable Git fixture and the public repository.
risks.mitigation: After publishing, verify registration, install and refresh from the public GitHub source in both CLIs. Retain the disposable fixture to isolate catalog or manifest regressions.

risks.description: Copies diverge or relative assets disappear during packaging.
risks.mitigation: Generate from one allowlist and compare build output. Smoke-test both renderers from the installed skill directories after removing the source checkout.

risks.description: A standalone install encounters a missing scope, conflicting file or interrupted copy.
risks.mitigation: Ask for missing scope in the agent flow. A noninteractive installer run requires explicit scope. Stage copies, detect divergent files and verify retry and cleanup behavior with temporary destinations.

risks.description: The working tree contains edits in both tovli-plan copies, so a generated package could publish work from the wrong copy.
risks.mitigation: Inventory both trees and resolve source differences with the maintainer before cutover. Build releases from the selected committed revision.

events.summary: Requested a plan for marketplace installs and agent-driven installation from the repo, with both Codex and Claude support.
Inspected the catalog and workspace copies, checked client documentation and local CLI help, and drafted options for grouping, install tooling, and client coverage.

Selected three named marketplace groups, a cross-platform installer invoked from a checkout, both routes on Codex CLI and Claude Code with desktop routes listed only after verification, and a scope question whenever omitted.

Checked that both CLIs document adding a Git marketplace at a specified ref. Added a first-step fixture to verify that three distinct marketplace names from the same repository can coexist, install and refresh in each client.
events.previous_value: Three named marketplace groups with client catalog layout to be verified.
events.new_value: Three distinct catalog registrations are required by the plan. Same-repo Git refs are the first proposed layout and remain unverified.

events.summary: Implemented the shared Git snapshot builder, three independent marketplaces, checkout installer and release guide. Verified both native CLIs against generated packages and ran the distribution regression suite on Windows and Ubuntu. Built a local 0.1.0 preview. Public release remains pending.

Published the source, v0.1.0 tag, and all three marketplace branches to GitHub in one atomic push. Verified fresh public installs in both CLI clients and ran the seven distribution tests from the public tagged checkout.

versions.change_summary: Initial plan covering both install routes, client coverage choices, and release acceptance checks.
Applied the user’s four decisions and updated the marketplace, installer, scope, and validation plans.
Made separate marketplace registration a release check and added the Git ref validation and fallback. Preserved the four decisions recorded in v2.
Recorded the implemented installer and builder, local validation, and the remaining public release checks.
Recorded GitHub publication and verified public CLI installations.

diagrams.title: How users get to an installed skill
diagrams.description: Users add one of the three marketplaces for a native install or give the agent the repo URL to run the cross-platform installer. Both routes end with skill discovery and invocation.
